title: Two sides of the page
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Are you the person who sees the future, or the person who gets today's tasks done?
A student said what the person learned from a conflict with a partner: being a hardcore boss isn't always the best way to get things done.

Imagine you draw a line down the middle of a page, I said. On one side is the mad scientist: visionary, intuitive, goal-oriented, seeing the future. On the other side are the operational people who help you get there. There will always be that division.

I used the personality test: intuitive people and sensors. Sensors are in the here and now. A person with fifty things to do today gets great anxiety from someone who only talks about the future of banking.
We have to learn to balance that, I said.
He gets on a mission, I said, and on the way he finds little nuggets of gold. You have a vision for a business and on the road you find an opportunity: oh my God, I didn't see this.

My example: a payment system built on email that became the core business, and a company that wanted to colonize another planet found itself with a satellite business. The road takes you off the road, I said, to a destination where you say: I just found something.

A student said: it's impossible for one person to have the balance, and that's why working as a team is good. If nobody is taking risks and thinking like a visionary, there won't be big next tasks. And the other way around.
I said I have seen what happens to a company when the innovation leaves and only corporate people doing daily tasks are left.
Which side of the page are you on, and who is on the other?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write which side of the page you are on: visionary or operational.
Write who is on the other side in your work.
Write the one thing each of you finds hard about the other.
Write a nugget of gold you found on the way to something else.
Write how you will share the balance.

check.q: How did I describe the visionary side?
choices: Mad scientist, intuitive, goal-oriented, seeing the future

check.q: What did a student say about balance?
choices: It's impossible for one person; that's why teams are good
One person can do it all

check.q: What did I call the opportunities found along the way to a mission?

recap: Know your side of the page. Build a team that covers the other.
